about.title: About Pragmatic UX Design
about.subtitle: Pragmatic UX Design emerged from real-world challenges in product development, where traditional UX processes often clashed with business realities.
about.sectionTitleAudience: Who it's for & what we address
about.forWhoBullet1: UX designers and product managers who want to work pragmatically
about.forWhoBullet2: Development teams who want to integrate UX methods meaningfully
about.forWhoBullet3: Stakeholders who want UX impact without "process for process's sake"
about.problemsBullet1: UX is seen as a bottleneck or documentation overhead
about.problemsBullet2: Too little time or budget for "perfect" processes
about.problemsBullet3: Unclear which methods fit your project and context
about.problemsBullet4: Rigid UX frameworks clash with real deadlines and team realities
about.originText: Pragmatic UX Design was developed through hands-on experience working on diverse projects at Ergon, where I encountered teams with varying UX maturity, timelines, and constraints. Rather than forcing a one-size-fits-all approach, I learned to adapt UX methods to each unique context.
about.philosophyText: Pragmatic UX Design isn't about cutting corners, it's about being strategic. It's the result of countless projects where I discovered that the most impactful UX work happens when we focus on what truly matters for users and business goals, rather than following rigid processes.
about.articleText: This website emerged from the Medium article
about.articleName: Pragmatic UX: Maximising Impact Without Overcomplicating Design
about.articleDescription: The article explores the core principles and practical approaches that form the foundation of this methodology. Read the full article to dive deeper into the concepts, real-world examples, and the thinking behind each principle.
